messages:
alex: Quick follow-up after yesterday's RFC — we left the edge behavior for mid-stream failures underspecified. specifically: if backend has started producing tokens and the client disconnects or a backend error happens, do we try transparent replay, return partial+error with a resume token, or close and force full retry?

maria: I'd avoid transparent replay. model state isn't trivially rewindable (kv cache, attention states). replay risks divergence and hidden nondeterminism.

dmitri: What about issuing a compact resume token at the last acknowledged fragment? header = x-rw-resume-token. then we can resume on same or compatible backend.

alex: That was suggested, but RFC didn't define token contents or storage. Do we inline cache snapshot in token (big) or store a pointer server-side?

ben: Proposal A: token = opaque id; backend persists small metadata (request-id, last-offset, model-variant, pointer to KV blob) in redis with TTL. On resume we lookup token and attach KV.

caroline: Storing per-request KV blobs in memory across millions of connections is a scaling bomb. A pointer->redis approach is ok but introduces extra RTT during resume.

maria: Tradeoffs: inline token = higher bandwidth on every response; server-side pointer = memory/disk cost + resume latency. choose depending on SLOs.

dmitri: Also need client-visible semantics: if we return partial + error and a resume token, clients can decide to resume instead of resending whole prompt. Without token they'll resend and possibly see duplicated output. so add idempotency header: x-rw-idempotency-key.

alex: Let's standardize these headers: x-rw-request-id, x-rw-idempotency-key, x-rw-resume-token, x-rw-resume-ttl. We'll document TTL defaults.

ben: We should also decide default behavior on connection loss: keep compute running for a window (so we can finish and stash token) vs abort immediately (wastes fewer GPU cycles).

caroline: Default = abort compute quickly (release GPU). Offer "continue_on_disconnect=true" as a tenant-level opt-in for Dedicated customers who pay to persist compute and want long-resume windows.

maria: For multi-region smart-routing: token must contain or point to the model hash/variant to avoid resuming on incompatible model. include model-hash in token metadata.

alex: For function-calling streams we need stronger checkpoints. treat function-call boundaries as safe checkpoint points: issue a token only after an event boundary so resuming won't corrupt structured outputs.

dmitri: Quick header schema (draft):
```json
{
  "x-rw-request-id": "uuid",
  "x-rw-idempotency-key": "optional-client-key",
  "x-rw-resume-token": "opaque-id",
  "x-rw-resume-ttl": "30s",
  "x-rw-model-hash": "sha256:abcd..."
}
```

ben: Implementation detail: token store TTL default = 30s, resume_window = 60s for Dedicated with continue_on_disconnect. Bench vs memory and redis needed.

caroline: I'll run perf benches: in-memory ephemeral store (per-proxy) vs redis cluster keyed by token for 100k concurrent short-lived tokens. expect memory wins on latency but loses on scale and failover.

maria: SDK change: expose resume_token + docs explaining client flow: if you receive partial + token, you may resume with same idempotency-key + token. SDK should dedupe on resume to avoid duplicated callbacks.

alex: Agreement checkpoint: converge on Proposal A (opaque token -> redis pointer with model-hash + offset). no transparent replay. default compute abort on disconnect. continue_on_disconnect opt-in for Dedicated. tokens TTL 30s default.

ben: I'll author a follow-up RFC fragment with costs and code sketches. who will own perf?

caroline: I'll own perf and post numbers next week.

maria: I'll update SDK drafts and client retry semantics section.

deploy-bot: edge-proxy v2.3.0 deployed to staging :rocket: (rollout: canary 25%)

dmitri: sounds good. after the perf numbers we can decide if token TTLs need tuning or if we should support a hybrid inline-token for tiny requests.

alex: Thanks everyone — I'll open the RFC PR with these decisions and link the perf issues.

alex: Closing this thread — please add objections inline on the PR.
